key: Not this way go I forth: hard is the passage. Forth from the side obliquely will I issue. Much that is yet undone must I accomplish; one must I combat and the other question.
s: The verse answers the first voice, which urges the old path of birth; Sāyaṇa, on 4.18.2, hears the sage Vāmadeva, still unborn, answering Indra, and takes the one to be fought as a rival, the one questioned as a seeker of knowledge.

evidence.gloss: Vāmadeva answers Indra, who had spoken so. I will not go out by this, the path of the womb; I will not go forth. This way, the going out from the womb, is hard to take, not to be reached. Rather I will go out from the side, obliquely: the meaning is, not having come out from the place of the womb, I will go out by breaking through the side. Not only this, which others have not done, is done by me: many deeds undone by others are mine to do. With one, a rival who disputes with me, let me fight; with one who wishes to know, let me question well.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 4.18.2, at [313,2]). Sāyaṇa on 4.18.2 opens: Vāmadeva answers Indra, who had spoken the first verse (he marks 4.18.1 indravākyam); he glosses the side exit as breaking through the side while not yet out of the womb (yonideśād anirgato ’ham), the one to be fought as sapatnena vivadamānena, a disputing rival, and the one questioned as bubhutsunā, one wishing to know. The hymn introduction he quotes calls Vāmadeva garbhastho jñānasaṃpanno mahāmuniḥ, and Wilson note 1 reports the same legend from Sāyaṇa. Plain sense faithful: 4.18.2 does answer 4.18.1, which commends the ancient path of birth; no four words of the key are repeated.
